items.followUp: Explain the formation of magnesium oxide by ionic bonding.

rubric.why: Sodium loses its outer electron during the formation of sodium chloride.
rubric.description: States that sodium transfers or loses one electron.
rubric.how: Award for describing the electron loss by sodium.

rubric.why: Chlorine accepts the electron transferred from sodium.
rubric.description: States that chlorine gains an electron.
rubric.how: Award for describing the electron gain by chlorine.

rubric.why: Electron transfer forms a positive sodium ion and a negative chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award when both the sodium and chloride ions are identified.

rubric.why: The attraction between oppositely charged ions is the ionic bond in sodium chloride.
rubric.description: Explains that the attraction between the ions forms the ionic bond in NaCl.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the ionic bond as the attraction between the ions, or naming the bond in NaCl.

modelAnswer: A sodium atom loses its outer electron, which is transferred to a chlorine atom.
Sodium forms a positive Na⁺ ion and chlorine forms a negative Cl⁻ ion.
The electrostatic attraction between these oppositely charged ions forms the ionic bond in sodium chloride (NaCl).

items.followUp: Differentiate between a monoatomic molecule and a polyatomic molecule, giving an example of each.

rubric.why: A homoatomic molecule contains atoms of the same element.
rubric.description: Defines a homoatomic molecule and may give an example.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its atoms are of the same element or giving a correct example such as O₂ or H₂.

rubric.why: A heteroatomic molecule contains atoms of different elements.
rubric.description: Defines a heteroatomic molecule and may give an example.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its atoms are of different elements or giving a correct example such as H₂O.

modelAnswer: A homoatomic molecule consists of atoms of the same element, for example O₂.
A heteroatomic molecule consists of atoms of different elements, for example H₂O.

items.followUp: Write the empirical formula of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, and explain how it is obtained.

rubric.why: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.description: Defines an empirical formula as the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it expresses the simplest whole-number ratio of the constituent atoms.

rubric.why: The empirical formula of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, is CH₂O.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of an empirical formula.
rubric.how: Award for giving CH₂O as the empirical formula of glucose.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
For example, the empirical formula of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is CH₂O.

rubric.why: Sodium and magnesium are in the same period, and magnesium has a greater nuclear charge.
rubric.description: Compares the position or nuclear charge of sodium and magnesium.
rubric.how: Award for stating that they are in the same period and magnesium has greater nuclear charge, or directly stating that magnesium has a greater nuclear charge or more protons.

accept: magnesium attracts its outer electron more strongly
more energy is needed to remove it
sodium has the lower ionization energy
rubric.why: Magnesium's outer electron is more strongly attracted, so it takes more energy to remove than sodium's outer electron.
rubric.description: Links the stronger attraction in magnesium with its higher ionization energy.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that magnesium's outer electron is more strongly attracted and requires more energy to remove, establishing that sodium has the lower ionization energy.

modelAnswer: Sodium and magnesium are in the same period, but magnesium has a greater nuclear charge.
Magnesium attracts its outer electron more strongly, so more energy is needed to remove it; therefore, sodium has the lower ionization energy.
